record.original_question: Let integers b ≥ a ≥ 2 be given, and let (A_i, B_i)_{i∈I} be a finite collection of pairs of finite sets such that |A_i| = a, |B_i| = b, and |A_i ∩ B_i| = 2 for every i, and such that A_i ∩ B_j is not contained in A_k ∩ B_k for all i ≠ j and all k. Must one have |I| ≤ Σ_{i=2}^a 2^{i-2} * C(a+b-2i, a-i)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.2. Let b ≥ a ≥ 2 be integers and (Ai, Bi)i∈I be a collection of pairs of finite sets, indexed by a finite set I, with the following properties. 1. |Ai| = a, |Bi| = b and |Ai ∩ Bi| = 2 for all i ∈ I. 2. Ai ∩ Bj 6⊆ Ak ∩ Bk for all i, j, k ∈ I with i 6= j. Then |I| ≤ Σ_a_{i=2} 2^{i−2} (a+b−2i choose a−i).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $b \geq a \geq 2$ be integers. Let $I$ be a finite index set, and let $\{(A_i, B_i) : i \in I\}$ be a collection of pairs of finite sets satisfying the following conditions:

1. For every $i \in I$, $|A_i| = a$, $|B_i| = b$, and $|A_i \cap B_i| = 2$.
2. For all $i, j, k \in I$ with $i \neq j$, the set $A_i \cap B_j$ is not a subset of $A_k \cap B_k$.

Prove or disprove the following: under these hypotheses,
$$|I| \;\leq\; \sum_{i=2}^{a} 2^{i-2} \binom{a+b-2i}{a-i}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated as a conjecture generalizing the Bollobás Two Families Theorem with a fixed-size intersection condition. Web searches did not surface any resolution or partial progress on this exact bound; it appears to remain an open conjecture.
